concepts.why: The patient presents with right iliac fossa pain, nausea, and diarrhea, and the abdominal CT scan shows a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole with a pericecal collection, which is consistent with appendicitis.
The patient has a history of laparoscopic appendectomy and presents with a pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips, which suggests a postoperative abscess.
The patient presents with right lower quadrant pain and elevated C-reactive protein level, which could be consistent with diverticulitis.
The patient is febrile and has an elevated white-blood-cell count with neutrophilia, which suggests an intra-abdominal infection.
The abdominal CT scan shows a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole, which suggests cecal inflammation.
The patient has a history of laparoscopic appendectomy and presents with a pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips, which suggests a surgical site infection.
The patient presents with right lower quadrant pain and the abdominal CT scan shows a pericecal collection, which suggests a right lower quadrant abscess.
The abdominal CT scan shows a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole with a pericecal collection, which suggests pericecal inflammation.

rationales.F01: Right iliac fossa pain is a common symptom of appendicitis and cecal inflammation.
rationales.F08: A swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole is highly suggestive of appendicitis or cecal inflammation.
rationales.F09: A pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips is highly suggestive of a postoperative abscess.
